note: Riddle bank for Insights of the Day v3. One per mail, in order; the answer opens the next mail. Plain hyphens only. Add new ones at the end.

riddles.q: I am a number, yet I am not a number, and I am not even equal to myself. What am I?
riddles.why: NaN == NaN is False, so use math.isnan() or pandas isna() to find missing values.

riddles.q: I remember every change you ever made and can take you back to any moment, but I am happiest when you commit. What am I?
riddles.why: Every commit is a save point you can return to with git checkout or git revert.

riddles.q: A model is 99% accurate at spotting fraud, yet it has never caught a single fraudster. How?
riddles.why: On imbalanced data, accuracy lies. Check precision and recall instead.

riddles.q: A bat and a ball cost 1.10 in total. The bat costs 1.00 more than the ball. How much is the ball?
riddles.why: Ball 0.05 + bat 1.05 = 1.10. Fast thinking says 0.10; slow thinking checks the sum.

riddles.q: In Python, what does 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 return?
riddles.why: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 in floating point. Compare with math.isclose().

riddles.q: I ship everywhere and carry everything an app needs, yet I never touch water. What am I?
riddles.why: A Docker container bundles the app with its dependencies, so it runs the same on any machine.

riddles.q: Five machines make five widgets in five minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 widgets?
riddles.why: Each machine makes one widget in 5 minutes, however many machines run in parallel.

riddles.q: In SQL, what does NULL = NULL return?
riddles.why: Any comparison with NULL is unknown. Use IS NULL to test for it.

riddles.q: I learn your history perfectly, every bump and wiggle, but show me tomorrow and I fall apart. What am I?
riddles.why: Overfitting memorises noise. Hold-out data and cross-validation catch it early.

riddles.q: Lily pads double in area every day. They cover the whole lake on day 48. On which day did they cover half?
riddles.why: One doubling before 'full' is 'half'. Exponential growth looks slow, then sudden.

riddles.q: How many people must be in a room for a better than even chance that two share a birthday?
riddles.why: There are 253 possible pairs among 23 people, so a match becomes more likely than not.

riddles.q: I am a list that refuses to change. What am I?
riddles.why: Tuples are immutable, so they can be dictionary keys and are safe to share.

riddles.q: Three doors, one car, two goats. You pick door 1. The host, who knows, opens door 3: a goat. Should you switch to door 2?
riddles.hint: The host never opens the car door
riddles.why: Switching wins 2 times in 3. Your first pick keeps its 1 in 3 chance.

riddles.q: I am the median of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 100. My friend the mean is much bigger. What are we?
riddles.hint: One outlier pulls only one of us
riddles.why: Outliers drag the mean, not the median. Report the median for skewed data like salaries or latency.

riddles.q: What has keys but opens no locks, has space but no room, and lets you enter but never go inside?
riddles.why: Keys, a space bar and an Enter key.

riddles.q: I am a forest without a single leaf, yet my trees vote to make predictions. What am I?
riddles.why: Many decision trees, each trained on a random sample, vote together. The crowd beats a single tree.

riddles.q: In Git, which command finds commits you thought you had lost after a bad reset?
riddles.hint: A log of where HEAD has been
riddles.why: The reflog records every move of HEAD for weeks, so 'lost' commits are usually one checkout away.

riddles.q: There are 10 kinds of people: those who understand binary and those who do not. How many kinds is that?
riddles.why: 10 in binary is 2 in decimal.

riddles.q: In Python 3, what does round(2.5) return?
riddles.why: Python rounds halves to the nearest even number (banker's rounding), so round(3.5) is 4.

riddles.q: Which SQL count skips the empty cells: COUNT(*) or COUNT(column)?
riddles.hint: One counts rows, one counts values
riddles.why: COUNT(*) counts every row; COUNT(column) ignores NULLs. Mixing them up skews averages.

riddles.q: Which is bigger: 0.999... (nines forever) or 1?
riddles.why: 3 x 0.333... = 0.999... and 3 x 1/3 = 1. Same number, two spellings.

riddles.q: I am the curve you want the most area under. What am I?
riddles.why: Area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 1.0 is perfect ranking; 0.5 is a coin flip.

riddles.q: In Python, is 'apple' < 'Banana' True or False?
riddles.hint: Capital letters come first in the code table
riddles.why: Uppercase letters sort before lowercase, so 'Banana' comes first. Sort with key=str.lower.

riddles.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
riddles.why: A classic to warm up the brain.

riddles.q: Treatment A wins in every age group, yet loses when you add the groups together. How can that be?
riddles.hint: Look at how many patients each group has
riddles.why: Uneven group sizes can flip a trend when data is combined. Always check the subgroups.

riddles.q: I start counting at 0 while you count from 1, and together we break your loop. What am I?
riddles.why: Index 0 vs 1 and < vs <= cause most boundary bugs. Test the first and last item.

riddles.q: What is the average time to look up a key in a Python dict, however big it gets?
riddles.why: Dicts use hashing, so lookups stay fast. Searching a list is O(n).

riddles.q: In a regular expression, which single character matches any character except a newline?
riddles.why: Use \. to match a real full stop.

riddles.q: Which cron schedule runs every single minute?
riddles.why: Minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week: all stars means every minute.

riddles.q: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They catch three fish and each gets exactly one. How?
riddles.why: The father is both a father and a son, so there are only three people.

riddles.q: How many times can you subtract 5 from 25?
riddles.why: After the first time you are subtracting from 20, not 25.

riddles.q: You run SELECT without ORDER BY twice. Is the row order guaranteed to be the same?
riddles.why: Without ORDER BY the order can change with plans, parallelism or updates. Always sort explicitly.

riddles.q: Which grows faster for big n: n squared or 2 to the power n?
riddles.why: At n = 20, n squared is 400 while 2^20 is 1,048,576. Exponential beats polynomial.

riddles.q: In Python, what do [] == [] and [] is [] return?
riddles.hint: Equal is not the same as identical
riddles.why: == compares values; 'is' checks for the same object in memory. Use 'is' only for None.

riddles.q: I have many layers, I am built from a file that starts with FROM, and containers are made from me. What am I?
riddles.why: Each Dockerfile step adds a layer. Put rarely changing steps first so the cache saves build time.

riddles.q: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish. What am I?
riddles.hint: You fold me or zoom me
riddles.why: A classic. Like a map, a good dashboard leaves out detail on purpose.

riddles.q: What value in Python is not zero, not False and not empty, yet still fails an if test?
riddles.why: None is falsy. Test it with 'if x is None' so a real 0 or empty string is not mistaken for missing.

riddles.q: Which HTTP status code means 'I'm a teapot'?
riddles.why: An April Fools' joke from 1998 (RFC 2324) that many web servers still recognise.

riddles.q: The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
riddles.why: A classic. In data, too much noise does the same to the signal.

riddles.q: Phil Karlton said there are only two hard things in computer science. Name them.
riddles.why: The joke version adds a third: off-by-one errors.

riddles.q: A coin lands heads 5 times in a row. What is the chance the next flip is heads?
riddles.why: Each fair flip is independent. Expecting tails 'is due' is the gambler's fallacy.

riddles.q: You test 20 useless features at a 5% significance level. How many look 'significant' by luck, on average?
riddles.why: Test many things and something always passes. Correct for multiple tests or confirm on new data.

riddles.q: What can travel around the world while staying in one corner?
riddles.why: A classic. Small things travel far, like a tip forwarded to a teammate.

riddles.q: Which tiny file tells Git which files never to track?
riddles.why: Add data files, .env files and secrets to it before your first commit, not after.

riddles.q: A dataset of 1,000 rows has 999 rows of 'No' and 1 'Yes'. You split it 80/20 at random. What can go wrong?
riddles.a: The 'Yes' may land in only one split
riddles.why: Use a stratified split (stratify=y in scikit-learn) so each split keeps the class balance.

riddles.q: What has a neck but no head, and wears a cap?
riddles.why: A classic. Like a bottleneck, the slowest step limits the whole pipeline.
